effort_evidence: Six opening fighter squadrons by type, a named I-15 squadron with Soviet pilots later at Brunete, and two December escort squadrons at Tremp.
loss_evidence: The nine-aircraft bomber sortie has three documented returns to friendly fields. Fighter losses for the campaign remain open.
effect_evidence: Survivor accounts and command action document the consequences of the break in escort.

effort_evidence: The Italian chronology names two initial and four arriving squadrons. Spanish and German accounts identify other reinforcements, with the opening third Fiat squadron unresolved.
loss_evidence: The 2G3 combat account describes attacks, including one without an observed outcome. A complete reciprocal loss ledger is missing.
effect_evidence: Italian and Spanish command correspondence documents demand for air support. The Tremp accounts establish contact without allocating every bomber loss.

effort_evidence: The Pursuit Brigade report and Army Modlin account document distinct morning and afternoon participation.
loss_evidence: The commander’s 16:00 report tracks the first day. IPN later distinguishes destroyed and damaged aircraft by airfield and period, including the move to Lublin.
effect_evidence: A formation dispersed in front of III/1. Jabłonna was bombed, and a separate 3 September report documents a shutdown at the Okęcie airframe works.

effort_evidence: Three German bomber Staffeln and a separate fighter sweep are identifiable on 1 September. Of two later Slovak fighter detachments at Kamenica, one has competing identifications.
loss_evidence: A Slovak fighter force-landed on 9 September and its pilot later escaped. German losses claimed by the Pursuit Brigade remain incompletely matched.
effect_evidence: One Staffel bombed Ciechanów while the others met Polish fighters. Slovak fighter escort is documented without a measured ground result.

effort_evidence: Norwegian Army fighters, Norwegian naval aviation, shore- and carrier-launched British naval aircraft and the Bardufoss RAF squadrons can be distinguished.
loss_evidence: Fornebu airframe records follow individual Gladiators. A coalition-wide loss total with common damage criteria remains open.
effect_evidence: The Bergen sinking has a German recipient record. The 28 May patrols coincided with the Allied assault at Narvik.

effort_evidence: Gaul’s schedule identifies two initial fighter groups, an additional group on 15 April, and eleven initial level- or dive-bomber groups.
loss_evidence: The German naval diary establishes the loss of Königsberg. The Grotli account identifies a specific He 111. Neither gives theatre-wide aircraft losses.
effect_evidence: The cruiser’s surviving crew transferred to coastal defence. The sortie from Ark Royal can be tied to the interruption of one German bombing attack.

effort_evidence: Named French, Dutch, Belgian, Polish and RAF formations have separate command and date boundaries.
loss_evidence: Vroenhoven yields three escort aircraft outcomes. The Polish roster identifies individual fatalities. French, Dutch and British returns still need a common daily basis.
effect_evidence: At Schiphol some fighters refuelled and flew again. Survivors regrouped at Buiksloot. Belgian escort losses can be traced through the aircraft that actually returned.

effort_evidence: The Luftflotte 2 table identifies seven Bf 109 and four Bf 110 Gruppen in one fighter-command section. Other corps and Luftflotte 3 enlarge the theatre total.
loss_evidence: German assignments and combined headquarters strength do not identify losses. The June Polish claims lack reciprocal German loss returns.
effect_evidence: I./JG 1 removed two of three Belgian escorts over Vroenhoven. Evidence for the bridge strike itself belongs to the bomber and recipient records.

effort_evidence: Six 7 September squadron records distinguish guarding, contact and launch. The 15 September chronology distinguishes scramble orders from airborne status.
loss_evidence: Beard’s damaged Hurricane and bailout are reported by No. 249. No. 72’s later observation of hits gives no verified German loss.
effect_evidence: The Admiralty records fires in four dock systems. The museum ties a single 15 September interception to the Dornier that fell at Victoria Station.

effort_evidence: A contemporary I. Fliegerkorps order specifies three bomber wings, three escort wings and a separate clearance wing. It supplies no actual sortie count.
loss_evidence: The British accounts contain claims and isolated aircraft outcomes. They do not reconstruct each German wing’s losses or repairable damage.
effect_evidence: London docks sustained major fires despite interception. No witness assigns the damage at each dock to one German wing.

effort_evidence: 74 allocated squadrons in nine roles. RAF history counts 2,614 RAF and USAAF sorties over the operation, including seven Coastal Command sorties.
loss_evidence: The RAF narrative reports 106 aircraft lost in its own force categories. Three No. 403 aircraft failed to return from its first patrol. All twelve returned from its second.
effect_evidence: The naval commander credited the cover. No. 411 observed a bomber release about a mile from the convoy, while HMS Berkeley was disabled by bombing and scuttled.

effort_evidence: Six identified fighter Gruppen and two dedicated fighter-bomber Staffeln. British wireless intelligence counted at least 86 long-range bombers. A complete German strike and reconnaissance order remains open.
loss_evidence: German records summarized by the RAF list 25 bombers and 23 fighters destroyed, plus 16 bombers and eight fighters damaged. Crew combat claims have a separate basis.
effect_evidence: German ground observers reported that smoke obscured landing craft. German attacks reached the shipping. The naval diary confirms the loss of Berkeley without identifying the attacking unit.

effort_evidence: Nos. 185 and 249 supplied timed approach patrols on 15 August. Indomitable’s campaign return covers a separate carrier effort.
loss_evidence: Indomitable reported eight aircraft lost and four pilots saved during Pedestal. On Malta, two No. 229 Spitfires were damaged in a landing collision on 15 August.
effect_evidence: The port’s 16 August signal records unloading from five ships including Ohio. The island patrols document cover during the approach.

effort_evidence: The Italian 13:00 wave on 12 August sent 43 torpedo aircraft. Two turned back. Two fighter groups provided escort.
loss_evidence: The Italian account identifies the 109° commander’s ditched S.79 and one 2° Gruppo Re.2001 shot down.
effect_evidence: Mattesini found no torpedo hit from this wave. Other attacks on the convoy continued and the ship damage return does not assign every hit to a unit.

effort_evidence: No. 92 recorded 42 sorties from Malta on 10 July and 41 on the transition day of 13 July. The US command separately reported 36 A-36s against Milazzo on 25 July.
loss_evidence: The squadron recorded two missing pilots on 10 July, then a trawler rescue and one confirmed death. On 16 August it recorded Brendan Baker missing from a separate escort.
effect_evidence: Pachino patrols operated before the ground party arrived. At Messina the diary identifies escorted strike formations, but the German ferry damage lacks an attacking unit.

effort_evidence: The 10 July strength table distinguishes island and mainland or Sardinian Gruppen, plus night and ground-attack forces. It supplies no sorties by unit.
loss_evidence: The ferry diary identifies F 607 and two damaged Siebel ferries on 16 August. SF 175’s wrecking time differs between the translated night entry and the craft register.
effect_evidence: Bombing closed the Salvatore jetty. The ferry command shifted embarkation and finished its final crossings the following morning.

effort_evidence: Force V logged 265 carrier sorties on 9 September 1943. The AHB separately gives 796 land-based fighter sorties that day. South African roles are documented again in the April 1945 offensive.
loss_evidence: 886 Squadron lost Sub-Lt Prentice on approach to Attacker. The Force V account records 32 aircraft written off across the carrier operation.
effect_evidence: Offshore cover remained necessary while artillery denied Montecorvino. A new strip near Paestum went into service on 13 September. By April 1945 fighter-bombers were participating in the Senio offensive.

effort_evidence: On 9 September the German return records 82 fighter sorties and 26 ground-attack sorties. Separate German and Republican Italian returns give strengths for 20 August 1944.
loss_evidence: The 12 September naval chronology records one aircraft lost from the II./KG 100 attack. No comparable German loss total for all Salerno fighters is established here.
effect_evidence: On 11 September III./KG 100’s attack forced Savannah to withdraw from supporting the landing force. The later fighter strength tables alone cannot establish effects over the ground front.

effort_evidence: An identified 46th Fighter Regiment flight on 22 June and the front’s acknowledgment that two named bomber regiments received no task on 22–24 June.
loss_evidence: Southwestern Front recorded 237 aircraft destroyed or damaged on its fields over three days. No destroyed-only total is supplied here.
effect_evidence: Fifth Army’s 23 June order names 22nd Mechanized Corps as the intended beneficiary. The front air commander later acknowledged late ground support.

effort_evidence: Three JG 54 Gruppen and two attached Staffeln have readiness figures. Romanian combat grouping readiness covers all roles.
loss_evidence: No unit-level Axis loss is matched to the specific 46th Regiment flight.
effect_evidence: The opposing front records combined damage over three days. Attribution among German attacks remains open.

effort_evidence: The 22 November Soviet table gives holdings by air army; aircraft sent on individual interception missions remain untraced here.
loss_evidence: No Soviet loss return is matched to Romania’s 9–18 September fighter claims.
effect_evidence: The effect of Soviet interception on individual unsuccessful transport flights is unresolved.

effort_evidence: Romanian evidence gives 524 fighter sorties on 9–18 September. November transport records separate departures or commitments from arrivals.
loss_evidence: The Romanian military-history study reports 11 aircraft lost on 9–18 September, but its itemised types account for ten. The difference remains open.
effect_evidence: German bomber crews assessed Romanian escort positively. On 16 December Sixth Army’s quartermaster recorded 125 tons arriving and asked for more food.

effort_evidence: Northern 16th Air Army reported 1,232 sorties on 5 July. The southern 417 counts aircraft in a two-army attack.
loss_evidence: The 54th Guards account identifies one pilot’s Yak-7 catching fire. Soviet aggregate first-day losses cover several commands.
effect_evidence: Central Front ordered air and tank cooperation. The northern air army’s own history acknowledges inadequate support to the ground forces.

effort_evidence: The northern strike and reconnaissance orders name Gruppen and Staffeln on 4 July. They give no 5 July sortie denominator.
loss_evidence: XLVIII Panzer Corps’s memoir describes losses to Soviet aviation without a matched number of aircraft or tanks.
effect_evidence: On the main northern axis 16th Air Army’s account records a 6–8 km German penetration. The share explained by air support remains unknown.

effort_evidence: A French regiment’s 23 June escort and the receiving front’s 877 assault/bombing sorties are separately documented.
loss_evidence: The 24th Bomber Regiment lost the lead Pe-2 during the 27 June daytime bridge sortie. The evening mass strike reported no own losses.
effect_evidence: Front reports confirm cover and support. The air army identifies 9th Tank Corps as beneficiary of 569th Regiment’s daytime attack.

effort_evidence: A 26 June station list adds eight short-range reconnaissance Staffeln across three commands. Sorties by each remain open.
loss_evidence: German aircraft withdrawals in the existing records cover the month. They cannot validate losses on the Bobruisk mission.
effect_evidence: Ninth Army’s 27 June diary records road traffic halted at times and a courier carrying orders after bombing disrupted telephone communications.

effort_evidence: 16th Army recorded 2,545 day-fighter sorties on 16 April. The 18th Army gives 563 Berlin sorties on 25/26 April and 517 bombers reporting over the target.
loss_evidence: The 16th Air Army’s 16 April account lists 87 aircraft lost, 75 on combat tasks and 12 on other flights. On 25/26 April the 18th Air Army’s first corps separately reported two Il-4s missing.
effect_evidence: The Polish ground account dates the Oder crossings. The 18th Air Army’s city raid produced crew-observed fires without independent building or ground-unit returns.

effort_evidence: Two JG 4 Gruppen have named 19 April stations. The Soviet night report observed patrols but could not identify their units.
loss_evidence: A German unit loss return matching the 25/26 April Soviet bombing report has not been identified.
effect_evidence: Soviet crews observed fires and a German air response. German records tying these to a local command’s ability to fight remain open.

effort_evidence: The RCAF lists mission roles for 39 Canadian squadrons, including one on standby. RAF Nos. 38 and 46 Groups list 15 airborne squadrons.
loss_evidence: The Canadian return records one aircraft lost each for Nos. 426, 430 and 440, and two damaged for No. 440.
effect_evidence: Five gliders reached the Orne bridge objectives closely enough to put most of the assault force into immediate action.

effort_evidence: The 3 June strength table and 7 June transfer table separate troops already in the west from Gruppe reinforcements. The German June report describes small strike formations from Laval.
loss_evidence: Caldwell records one JG 26 FW 190 pilot lost on 6 June and a Mustang claimed. The 7–9 June transfer total gives no Gruppe-level loss return.
effect_evidence: The German June report records that daylight Allied air activity constrained German troop movement. The arrival dates alone cannot measure interceptions or damage inflicted.

effort_evidence: Day-one Dakota returns show crews released, tugs returned and gliders missing. On 19 September the dispatch group counted 163 aircraft off on resupply.
loss_evidence: The 19 September dispatch return counted 18 aircraft failing to return. The ground brigade separately recorded missing gliders in the first lift.
effect_evidence: The recipient’s 19 September accounts show 21 of 388 net tons gathered, with further unquantified collections possible.

effort_evidence: Luftflotte 3 recorded six prepared formations and three operating on 17 September. Caldwell identifies all three that flew.
loss_evidence: Caldwell separates one I./JG 26 FW 190 and pilot lost, two II./JG 26 pilots lost and III./JG 26 commander Mietusch killed. German victory claims have a different basis.
effect_evidence: The fighters engaged Allied escorts. Caldwell’s reconstruction found no German fighter reached the first lift transports. The British brigade recorded little opposition on its own flight.

effort_evidence: Polish combat reports give 31 departures by squadron and role. US 487th Fighter Squadron testimony gives an encounter beginning at takeoff.
loss_evidence: The Polish report separates 18 Spitfires destroyed on the ground, five damaged and two lost in air combat. Eindhoven repair categories distinguish 34 repaired Typhoons from 26 destroyed or beyond repair.
effect_evidence: Returning Polish fighters engaged the attackers at Ghent. Eindhoven repairs restored part of the Typhoon force, while the Evere ground crew recorded a fatality among its mechanics.

effort_evidence: The separate II. and III./JG 4 narratives and the four JG 26/JG 54 assignments distinguish launch, intended target and reported contact.
loss_evidence: Two II./JG 4 aircraft are identified in the Dutch register. Reconstructed JG 1 losses over Ghent do not identify victims of each Polish claim.
effect_evidence: German attackers struck occupied airfields at Evere, Eindhoven and Ghent. An assigned field could be lightly occupied, as Grimbergen was, or mistaken for a different field.

effort_evidence: The 6 March fighter table gives aircraft by group and escort stage. The Canadian return lists dispatches by aircraft type on 30/31 March.
loss_evidence: The Berlin fighter table reports eleven US fighters lost and identifies the groups. Nuremberg crew reports use a separate RAF night-raid population.
effect_evidence: The 100th Bombardment Group and 56th Fighter Group supply a local encounter. Night crews reported what they could see and whether they released or jettisoned.

effort_evidence: German operational maps and participant testimony identify the first and second Berlin concentrations. They leave other response stages outside these counts.
loss_evidence: Kretschmer of JG 1 describes his own bailout. His testimony cannot establish losses for the wing or reconcile Allied claims.
effect_evidence: The March 1944 naval diary records bombs falling across Berlin. In February 1945 German archive photographs document damage at specific streets and a station. Neither record attributes it to one escort or bomber group.

effort_evidence: The August plan names four P-47 groups. The October result names separate groups covering the two B-17 task forces and the B-24 rendezvous. Of 29 B-24s dispatched, only 21 flew the diversion.
loss_evidence: August losses split by route and group. Of 60 B-17s lost in October the headquarters account classed two as flak, eighteen as enemy aircraft and forty as cause unknown.
effect_evidence: Group records identify assigned works and early returns. The command's October estimate of industrial destruction can be checked against records from the factories.

effort_evidence: Five named night-fighter wings contributed elements in daylight in August. Two NJG 1 Gruppen can be followed by sortie. In October, five fighter divisions and competing command return totals are identified.
loss_evidence: Boiten records the return of damaged II./NJG 1 aircraft at St. Trond on 17 August. Contemporary confirmation decisions qualify the initial German claims. A loss roster for the entire October response remains open.
effect_evidence: The postwar industrial survey distinguishes September Schweinfurt output from the effect on German war production. The RAF history separates stock loss from machine damage.

effort_evidence: The Canadian Leipzig night roster, the 5th Wing's Steyr and Fiume assignment, two Gotha group records and four withdrawal fighter groups cover distinct operations.
loss_evidence: The Leipzig night count records missing Canadian crews. Steyr losses are separately bounded to the 5th Wing, and Gotha losses here cover the 445th Group.
effect_evidence: B-17 records distinguish Steyr from Fiume. Gotha post-strike photography documents structural damage. A briefing forecast supplies no measured production loss.

effort_evidence: The corps counted 362 fighters employed and 155 in combat on 20 February. A wider claims and casualty register identifies 27 Gruppen and their reported bases. The Austrian response on 24 February remains unresolved.
loss_evidence: Wood gives separate damage columns for German Gruppen on 20 February. III./ZG 26 alone has ten aircraft in the 60–100 percent bracket and three at lower damage. These figures cannot verify individual Allied claims.
effect_evidence: Steyr's municipal account distinguishes factory sections, casualties and housing losses. The evidence cannot disaggregate the effects of individual bomber or escort groups.
